case.title: The star that won't stay quiet
case.hook: Every few weeks, for a century of amateur records, it leaps fiftyfold in brightness in a day. Something is feeding on its neighbour.

query.adql: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_over_error, pmra, pmdec, ruwe, phot_g_mean_mag, phot_bp_mean_mag, phot_rp_mean_mag, bp_rp, phot_variable_flag, teff_gspphot, distance_gspphot, non_single_star, DISTANCE(POINT(325.67834770733,43.58607440069), POINT(ra,dec))*3600 AS sep_arcsec FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE 1=CONTAINS(POINT(ra,dec), CIRCLE(325.67834770733,43.58607440069,0.008333333333333333)) ORDER BY sep_arcsec

notes: rows_kept counts 6-month visits (W1 and W2), not exposures
observers (good points): SHPI:76939, JM:46811, ATE:40918, GFB:31550, PVA:30229, LMN:28682, LMA:26924, MXL:17524, CCHD:16685, JSJA:15231, BJAK:14525, HBB:12678
upper limits, discrepant (val=T) and non-standard bands are kept but flagged; visual estimates form their own series 'Vis.'
no ZTF source (target may be brighter than ZTF saturation, ~12.5 mag)
Sky Patrol light-curve service failed: ZeroDivisionError: integer modulo by zero

tess.archive: MAST TESS light curves via lightkurve
cuts: binned to 10-min medians per sector (good and flagged cadences kept apart)
notes: TESS magnitudes are relative (delta-mag vs each sector's median); sectors: 15, 16, 56, 76, 83

checks.title: Does AAVSO start at the star's normal brightness?
checks.finding: first 60 days of V: median 11.21; Gaia DR3 (2014-17 mean) implies V = 11.96; difference -0.75 mag. The series begins mid-event: its own median is not the star's normal state.
